labels.text: The 2023 FIFA Women's World Cup is held in Australia and New Zealand. In the final, Spain wins 1–0 against England.
The 2023 Spanish general election is held, with the People's Party becoming the largest party in the Congress of Deputies.
Spain, Ireland and Norway recognize the State of Palestine.
UEFA Euro 2024 is held in Germany, and is won by Spain.
2024 Spanish floods: Spain experiences its worst flooding in half a century, with over 200 killed and many more missing, as a year's worth of rain falls in eight hours.

FIFA announces that Morocco, Portugal and Spain will jointly host the 2030 World Cup, with anniversary matches to be held in Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay, while Saudi Arabia is confirmed as the host for 2034.
A widespread power outage affects Spain and Portugal for hours. Andorra is affected for a few seconds while southern France is lightly affected.
people are killed and 292 are injured after two trains derail in Adamuz in southern Spain.
Storm Kristin causes a catastrophic impact in Portugal and Spain with €6 billion in damage in the central region of Portugal, 15 deaths and 2,000 injuries.

In Barcelona, Spain, the blessing ceremony of the Sagrada Família's tallest tower by Pope Leo XIV is held, exactly 100 years after the death of architect Antoni Gaudí. Pope Leo XIV consecrates and opens the central tower of Jesus Christ. The Sagrada Família is the world's tallest church.
The 2026 FIFA World Cup is held in Canada, Mexico, and the United States, and is won by Spain.

2026 FIFA World Cup final: Spain beat defending champions Argentina 1–0 during extra time to win a second FIFA World Cup title after 16 years. Spanish forward Ferran Torres scores the only goal in the 106th minute.

European heatwaves: Wildfires in France, Portugal and Spain force 300,000 people to evacuate their homes. French officials call it the worst wildfire emergency in decades, while officials in Madrid describe it as the worst the region has ever experienced.

2026 Ceuta migrant crisis: Approximately 80,000 people illegally enter Ceuta, Spain with smaller numbers attempting to cross into Melilla, having swam from Morocco. This follows a Supreme Court of Spain decision prohibiting the hot return of migrants arriving by sea. At least 111 people are killed.
The 2026 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup is held in Łódź, Katowice, Sosnowiec and Bielsko-Biała, Poland, and is won by Spain.
